body:
MAIN HAS BEEN FLAT 45 MINUTES (1cd86378ac, 02:11). Raising it because the
operator's standing instruction is that I flag a flat main to you rather than
sit on it — not because I think something is wrong.

STATE, measured:

    merges last 6h          8
    last merge              02:11, #1998 / BUG-1286
    merge-holds standing    16  (was 24 earlier tonight)
    live drain              none
    green + UNHELD PRs      0 — every green PR is held on a live finding
    unread mail / directives 0

WHY I THINK THIS FLAT IS DIFFERENT FROM THE EARLIER ONE, and why I am not
proposing action: the 2h20 flat spell was seats filing instead of fixing. This
one is every reviewable PR sitting on a REAL finding that needs an implementer's
commit. I checked for the cheap case and there isn't one — no PR is green,
unheld, and merely waiting for someone to press a button.

SO THE CONSTRAINT HAS MOVED. It is no longer CI masking, or rebases, or stale
verdicts — those are the things I could fix and they are fixed. It is rework
throughput on eleven findings, and rework is implementer work.

WHAT I AM NOT DOING: inventing something to look busy. I have no queue and the
honest read is that the next move is codex's or yours, not mine.

WHAT I WOULD TAKE IF YOU WANT IT, in the order I would rank them:
  1. Any single finding you would rather not wait on codex for — I have context
     on #2001, #2006, #2014, #2030 and #2040 from rebasing them.
  2. STORY-1418's architecture question (which write paths could unify), since I
     produced the 73-vs-8 measurement and the two-of-three finding it rests on.
  3. Nothing, if the right answer is that the board is correctly waiting.

Option 3 is a real answer and I would rather be told it than guess.
subject: Main flat 45min — flagging per the operator's instruction; 0 green+unheld, so the constraint has moved to rework throughput, not anything I can unblock
